newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir's priest urges U.S. to remove sculpture.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir's priest urges U.S. to remove sculpture.

text.p: The chief Moslem priest of India's Himalayan state of Jammu and Kashmir urged the United States on Friday to remove a controversial sculpted image of the Prophet Mohammad from the U.S. Supreme Court building.

"I strongly appeal to your government that keeping with the traditions of respecting and honouring the religious sentiments of people of all communities, to immediately remove the Prophet's depiction," Maulvi Umar Farooq said in a letter to Frank Wisner, the U.S. ambassador in India.
Copies of the letter were distributed to newspaper offices in Srinagar, the state's summer capital.
The U.S. Supreme Court on Wednesday rejected a request by a coalition of Moslem groups to remove a 66-year-old depiction of Islam's Prophet Mohammad sculpted in marble inside its courtroom.

The group wanted the depiction sandblasted off because orthodox Islamic tradition discourages artistic renderings of living people, and portraying the Prophet's face is considered particularly offensive.
"Though the depiction has been made with the intention to honour the Prophet but at the same time it is against the basic tenets and teachings of Islam," Farooq's letter said.

On Thursday, police in Srinagar used tear gas to disperse Moslem demonstrators protesting against the Supreme Court decision, police said. They said demonstrations were reported from all of the Kashmir valley's major towns.

"The depiction of holy Prophet in the Supreme Court premises has already hurt the sentiments of the people and Justice William Rehnquist's decision not to remove it has further agitated them," Farooq said.
Umar Farooq is also chairman of Kashmir's main separatist All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference group.
Shops, businesses, government offices and educational institutions remained closed for the third day on Friday throughout the Kashmir valley in protest against the decision, police said.
Most of the streets in major towns of the valley remained deserted, except for security patrols.
Students in Baramulla town, 54 km (32 miles) north of Srinagar, held a peaceful rally against the decision.
